key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly enhance oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, while the high-entropy composition improves structural stability relative to LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: This study offers a materials-design route for oxide electrocatalysts used in water electrolysis, rather than solar-cell absorbers or AI systems.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probe structural defects, Ni valence, electronic states, and electrochemical OER performance.
Use first-principles calculations to interpret strain-dependent rare-earth–oxygen–nickel hybridization.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films show earlier OER onset and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the high-entropy nickelate also resists OER-induced structural degradation better than LaNiO3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and translating epitaxial-film results into scalable electrodes remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
